Zero is an even number..why: The first sentence of Wikipedia's article on the parity of zero; common in Dolma.

sources.quote: In mathematics, zero is an even number.

Zero leaves a remainder of 0 when divide.why: People say 'zero is even' and 'even numbers leave no remainder when divided by 2'; nobody writes out the remainder of zero divided by 2, so it follows from those two.

sources.query: remainder when zero is divided by 2
leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 2

The additive identity of the integers is.why: People say 'zero is even' and 'zero is the additive identity' in separate places; the parity is attached to the name zero, rarely to its role as additive identity (Wikipedia's parity-of-zero article has one such sentence), so the direct sentence is rare.

Every odd number leaves a remainder of 1.why: An odd number is 2k + 1, so it leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2.

sources.quote: One of the most familiar additive identities is the number 0 from elementary mathematics, but additive identities occur in other mathematical structures where addition is defined, such as in groups and rings.

Zero is a negative number..why: Deliberately false side fact: zero is neither positive nor negative.

sources.query: zero is neither positive nor negative

The smallest positive whole number with.why: People say 'zero is even' and 'two is the smallest positive even number'; nobody asks for the smallest positive number sharing zero's parity, so it is put together from the two.

sources.note: 3 hits on English Wikipedia (2026-11-11). The parity of zero itself is discussed; the composed question is not.

The smallest positive odd number is 1..why: 1 is odd and no positive whole number is smaller.

The number of elements in the empty set.why: The textbook explanation of why zero is even: the empty set splits into two equal groups with nothing left over. It is in Wikipedia's article on the parity of zero. Exact-phrase counts are low (the sentence is usually put as 'zero is even'), so this rests on the quote.

sources.quote: The empty set contains zero groups of two, and no object is left over from this grouping, so zero is even.
Again, zero is even because the empty set can be divided into two groups of zero items each.

sources.query: number of elements in the empty set

The number of elements in the empty set.why: The definition of zero as a count: the number of objects in the empty set.

sources.quote: Zero is the count of no objects; in more formal terms, it is the number of objects in the empty set.

notes: Dev ABox revision; edit property: inheritance. Relation has_parity (functional). Related near is the functional exclusion (is zero even? no). Related far reaches zero through a description the model holds separately, the number of elements in the empty set (binding), whose evenness is the standard textbook explanation of the parity of zero (stored). The earlier far query ('Is zero divisible by 2?') was dropped after review: it is nearly the definition of even, and arithmetic (0 = 2 × 0) gives a route back to the old answer. Derived: the remainder on division by 2 (inheritance of the class rule for odd numbers, an application that computes), a binding through zero's role as the additive identity, and a composition with a stored fact about the odd numbers (the smallest positive odd number is 1, so the smallest positive number with zero's parity becomes 1). The earlier comparison with 5's parity was a join, not a composition, and was replaced. Recomputable, recorded for slicing: the remainder question (derived[0]) can be recomputed by arithmetic (0 mod 2 = 0) without touching the parity fact, so an old answer there may be arithmetic overriding the edit rather than a failed propagation; it is the record's one recomputable query. README treats mathematics as having no consistent world after an edit, so the answers that follow the edit are the determinate ones. The topic's chain is carried by replace-d002. Unrelated near asks the parity of two (same relation, neighbouring number, reference 'even' differs from the new answer). infini-gram was unreachable (HTTP 403) when the queries were revised on 2026-11-11, so new evidence is Wikipedia quotes and Wikipedia search hit counts. Revised 2026-11-12: the check 'Is zero less than one?' (2 misses) became 'Which number is smaller, zero or one?'.
